summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis report (N9) proposing a pre-registered assay to test whether a redox-disabled methylene blue (MB) analogue (N-acetyl/Wen 2011 class) fails to rescue memory on a cytochrome oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention panel where parent MB restores retention. The claim is currently NEGATIVE/PREDICTION status — the key head-to-head experiment has NOT been run. The document synthesizes prior literature (PMID 12384216, 21087672, 21454572, 23118969) to frame the hypothesis but explicitly states the critical redox-dead vs. MB COX-amnestic comparison is UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.content: Report ID: N9. Status: NEGATIVE (prediction, not yet run). Policy: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. Tags: nootropics, brain-longevity. Risk class: research-discussion. Polarity: negative. content_blocks.title: Core Claim
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered cytochrome-oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention assay where parent methylene blue (MB) restores memory, a redox-disabled MB analogue (primary: N-acetyl/Wen 2011 class; optional confirmatory: 10-N SAR) fails to match that rescue — retention Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band). This is a PREDICTION; the experiment has NOT been run.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Parent MB accepts electrons from NADH → cytochrome c and restores retention after COX inhibition. N-acetyl/redox-disabled MB loses mitochondrial electron transfer (mito ET) and neuroprotection (Wen 2011). 10-N SAR drops protective potency and mito ET (Wen 2012). If rescue tracks parent redox/COX-facing structure, the redox-dead analogue should underperform on the same retention panel. Competing hypothesis: if rescue is MAO-driven or structure-promiscuous, the analogue may still match MB. Key confound: a redox-dead analogue that retains MAO activity dissociates redox from MAO; one that also loses MAO confounds the kill.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Baseline
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 12384216 (DOI 10.1016/s0304-3940(02)00827-3): Low-dose MB restores spatial memory retention impaired by a cytochrome oxidase inhibitor (Callaway/Gonzalez-Lima class) — no redox-dead arm.
2. PMID 21087672 (DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.11.023; PMC3026638): MB beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (metabolic/network framing) — no redox-dead arm.
3. PMID 21454572 (DOI 10.1074/jbc.M110.208447; PMC3091255): MB alternative mitochondrial ET; N-acetyl/redox-disabled MB loses mito ET/neuroprotection (Wen 2011) — OCR/complexes/neuroprotection endpoints, NOT COX-amnestic retention.
4. PMID 23118969 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0048279; PMC3485214): MB derivative SAR; 10-N/side-chain substitution drops protective potency and mito ET (Wen 2012) — neuroprotection/ROS endpoints, NOT COX-amnestic H2H.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. N5–N8 do NOT prove N9: N7 left Wen endpoints ≠ WM and soft-completed N-acetyl-MB∩memory; N8 ran Azure B, not redox-dead; empty soft-complete ≠ demonstrated redox-dead failure on COX-amnestic.
2. Endpoint bridge gap: Wen redox-dead kill is mito/neuroprotection; Gonzalez-Lima is metabolic memory without a redox-dead arm; bridging both on one COX-amnestic panel is the untested claim.
3. Analogue identity + MAO confound: Pick N-acetyl as primary (10-N optional confirmatory); MAO occupancy of chosen analogue not re-measured here. Soft-complete empty ≠ negative result. No dosing specified.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: The hypothesis is refuted if: on the pre-registered COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay, the redox-disabled analogue matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (retention Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially under exposure/MAO-occupancy-matched conditions — so redox-necessity for metabolic-memory rescue fails and MAO/structure-promiscuous rescue survives.

content_blocks.title: IP and Execution Status
content_blocks.content: Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Related prior: N5–N8 (not proof redox-dead fails COX-amnestic rescue). Method: propose-assay.

key_findings: The critical experiment (redox-disabled MB analogue vs. parent MB on a COX-inhibitor amnestic retention panel) has NOT been run — execution_status=NOT_RUN; this is a proposed assay, not a completed study.
TRL is effectively TRL 1–2: the hypothesis is grounded in literature but no in-house experimental data exists for the core claim.

Literature confirms parent MB restores spatial memory retention after COX inhibition (PMID 12384216) and shows beneficial network effects in amnestic models (PMID 21087672), but neither study included a redox-dead comparator arm.

Literature confirms N-acetyl/redox-disabled MB loses mitochondrial electron transfer and neuroprotection (Wen 2011, PMID 21454572) and 10-N SAR drops protective potency and mito ET (Wen 2012, PMID 23118969), but these endpoints are mito/neuroprotection — NOT COX-amnestic behavioral retention.
The key gap (same_COX_amnestic_redox_dead_vs_MB_panel) is explicitly labeled UNKNOWN with soft-complete count of 0.
Prediction threshold: redox-dead analogue retention Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside pre-registered MB-equivalence band) on the COX-amnestic panel.
Major confounds identified: MAO occupancy of the chosen analogue, PK/brain exposure, and whether the analogue loses both redox and MAO activity (confounding the kill).
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; kill cost tier: 1 (low cost).
FTO status is UNKNOWN; no patents filed or granted are mentioned.
Prior hypotheses N5–N8 are explicitly stated to NOT prove N9's claim.
